title: A Phenomenological Signature of Entropy Flow in Cosmic Structure Growth
content: The growth rate of large-scale structure, \(f\sigma_8(z)\), is a fundamental probe of gravity and dark energy. Next-generation surveys—DESI, Euclid, and CSST—will measure it with sub-percent precision, enabling searches for deviations from the standard ΛCDM model. We introduce a minimal phenomenological model in which structure growth is enhanced by an effective entropy flow, motivated by the thermodynamic interpretation of gravitational collapse. Its back-reaction on geometry modifies the linear perturbation equation by a single term \(\beta(a)H^2\), with \(\beta(a)=\beta_0(H/H_0)^{1/3}\). This specific redshift dependence breaks the degeneracy with the matter density \(\Omega_m\), allowing the model to be distinguished from ΛCDM and other modified gravity theories through multi-redshift measurements. For a fiducial value \(\beta_0=0.021\), the model predicts a 6.4% enhancement in \(f\sigma_8\) at \(z=0\). A comprehensive Fisher forecast, incorporating realistic correlated systematic errors and full marginalization over \(\{\Omega_m,\sigma_8,h\}\), shows that the combined DESI+Euclid+CSST data can constrain \(\sigma(\beta_0)=0.0012\), corresponding to a detection significance exceeding \(5\sigma\) (\(S/N\approx 17.5\)). This work translates a thermodynamic perspective on gravity into a concrete, falsifiable prediction for imminent observational data.
